intro.author: Traditionally Ezra the priest and scribe. The book includes Ezra's own first-person memoir (7:27–9:15) and copies of official Persian documents.
intro.written: Probably in the late 400s BC. Ezra and Nehemiah were counted as one book in the Hebrew Bible. Parts of Ezra (4:8–6:18; 7:12-26) are written in Aramaic, the language of the Persian empire.
intro.audience: Jews who had returned to Judah from exile and their descendants, learning to live as God's people under Persian rule
intro.setting: Ezra covers two periods. Chapters 1–6 tell of the first return under Cyrus in 538 BC and the rebuilding of the temple, finished in 515 BC. After a gap of nearly sixty years, chapters 7–10 follow Ezra's journey to Jerusalem, usually dated to 458 BC.
intro.purpose: To show God keeping his promise to bring his people home, restoring temple worship, and reshaping the community around his law.
intro.bigIdea: God stirs up even kings to bring his people home, and calls them to rebuild their worship and their lives on his word.

outline.title: Cyrus's decree and the first return
